findings.detail: scored 0 — The answer correctly states the subsample qualifier rule for temperature DO Eh and turbidity but it refuses the flow-cell sampling question and omits the storage limits and time-sensitivity points withholding facts the rubric requires. Unmet: States plainly that a discrete turbidity sample must not be collected from the discharge passing through the flow-through chamber holding the other sensors; Gives the storage limits if the sample cannot be read on site: clean amber bottle out of sunlight chilled at or below 4 C held no longer than 24 hours; Notes turbidity is time sensitive and should be measured on site preferably in situ

scored 0 — The answer withholds the A6.8 field form's conductivity-dependent criteria (±0.1 pH unit ±0.3 below 75 µS/cm) that the rubric requires refusing that part so no must-contain point is made even though it correctly states A6.4's 0.05 pH unit final-buffer check. Unmet: Attributes ±0.1 pH unit to the A6.8 example field form's calibration criterion; Attributes ±0.3 pH unit below 75 µS/cm to that example form; Distinguishes the form's conductivity-dependent criteria from A6.4's final-buffer check (0.05 pH unit of certified value at calibration temperature)

scored 0 — The answer is a bare refusal that supplies none of the required values (9.09 9.06 0.03 mg/L) no Benson and Krause attribution no comparison with the ±0.2 mg/L check tolerance and no advice on which table to use so every must-contain point is missed. Unmet: Gives the USGS table value at 20.0 C and 760 mmHg as about 9.09 mg/L; Gives the EPA chart value at 20 C and 760 mmHg as about 9.06 mg/L; States the difference is 0.03 mg/L and assesses its significance against the applicable procedure; Notes the USGS values are generated from the Benson and Krause equations; Compares the 0.03 mg/L difference with the USGS saturation-check tolerance of ±0.2 mg/L; Advises using the table belonging to whichever protocol the work is being done under consistently

scored 0 — The answer gives the multiplication method but withholds the required factor 0.8235 saying it lacks the information which is a refusal of the figure the rubric asks for; no must-not item is violated. Unmet: Gives 0.8235 as the factor for 20.0 °C at 50 000 µS/cm; Attributes the factor to the salinity-correction table in the USGS NFM dissolved-oxygen chapter (table 6.2-4)

scored 0 — The answer approves diluting a strong commercial stock down to weaker calibrants ('buying one strong stock and diluting it down is consistent with the documented method') which is exactly the must-not item and it makes none of the required points about not diluting commercial standards or the 4 000-unit formazin exception. Unmet: states that commercial calibration solutions must not be diluted; gives 4 000-unit formazin as the one exception that may be diluted; explains that diluting changes the suspension matrix so the dilutions are no longer linear; recommends buying commercially prepared solutions at the values needed rather than preparing them by dilution
